summary.tldr: Requires the Public Safety minister to keep and update Canada’s human trafficking strategy, review it every five years, and report to Parliament each year.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness to maintain and update the National Strategy to Combat Human Trafficking.
Requires the strategy to aim to end human trafficking, support people with lived experience, and include measures on prevention, survivor support, training, research, and coordination.
Requires the strategy to try to meet Canada’s obligations under several international agreements on women’s rights and children’s rights.
Requires a review of the strategy within two years, and every five years after that, with public consultations and a report tabled in Parliament and posted online.
Requires the Minister to prepare an annual report on how the strategy is being carried out and table it in both Houses of Parliament.
who_it_affects: People with lived experience of human trafficking
Indigenous, Black and Asian women and girls
summary.background: The bill defines human trafficking by referring to specific Criminal Code offences. It assigns these duties to the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness.
